title: What the average leaves out
hints: Liquid formation requires a phase-change contribution.
Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
solution: The gas-phase inventory does not account for the enthalpy of condensation to the liquid.
statement:
Why does a gas-phase bond enthalpy estimate using water as product differ from a standard reaction value with liquid water?

[_]{a}

choices: Condensation contributes an additional enthalpy change.
Water has no O–H bonds in the liquid.
The atom count changes on condensation.
All average bond energies give exact reaction values.
explanations: The specified phase matters in thermochemistry.
Liquid water still contains water molecules.
Bond strengths vary with chemical environment.
